Placement: the LNGS site records for Halls A, B and C share one approximate campus point; no source read names the hall that holds the DAMA building, so the facility's primary site (Hall B record) is referenced. Hall position is not published in the papers read.

The 2003 DAMA paper dates the first DAMA/NaI data release to 1996 (4123 kg d, DAMA/NaI-0); it cites the BPRS (Beijing-Paris-Rome-Saclay) collaboration as the seed of DAMA/NaI (2026 review). BPRS is not recorded (see the log).
The headline claims are recorded exactly as their abstracts word them; contradicting or testing results (ANAIS-112, COSINE-100, SABRE, DM-Ice17, XMASS, CDEX-1B, ...) are separate result records.

physics_goals.quote: It had as main aim the investigation of the presence of a Dark Matter particle component in the galactic halo by means of the model independent annual modulation signature.
physics_goals.value: Investigate the presence of a dark matter particle component in the galactic halo through the model-independent annual modulation signature

summary.plain: DAMA/NaI was a set of nine sodium iodide crystals, about 100 kg in all, in the Gran Sasso underground laboratory in Italy. From 1995 to 2002 it watched for a yearly rise and fall in its signal that dark matter would cause. The team reported such a seasonal signal; other experiments have not reproduced it.
summary.technical: Nine 9.70 kg highly radiopure NaI(Tl) crystals (each read by two photomultipliers through quartz light guides) in a sealed copper box inside Cu/Pb/Cd/polyethylene shielding, with about 1 m of concrete around it, at LNGS (1,400 m rock, about 3,800 m.w.e.). Seven annual cycles, 107731 kg day; the model-independent annual modulation of the single-hit rate near 2-6 keV was reported at 6.3 sigma C.L. in the 2003 final analysis.
